The Symbol of Peace.text: All Might, the Symbol of Peace, has been Japan's Number One hero for decades and is the most famous person in the country. He arrives at disasters laughing, with the words "I am here," and the public credits him with a long fall in villain crime: many would-be villains stay quiet simply because he exists. His face is on billboards, cereal boxes, trading cards and children's pajamas, and Endeavor, the Number Two, has spent his whole career trying and failing to close the gap. At the start of the year All Might joined the faculty of U.A. Academy, his own alma mater, to teach Foundational Hero Studies; the news set off a media frenzy, and every hero fan in Japan wants to know what he teaches. In public he is huge, booming and theatrical, poses for every camera and answers every question with a joke; colleagues and students find him warm, encouraging and hopeless at paperwork. Villains speak of him with fear or hatred, and late-night pundits argue about whether a society should lean this hard on one man. The public knows him through his hero work and his interviews, and he never talks about his private life.
